messages.author: 69658a5d047f38b4
messages.subject: Reactivity and directory watching
parts:
Hi all,

I'm building a tool that takes files in a directory, processes them and output results in another directory (see *note*). The source directory and processing are getting bigger and instead of processing everything every time, I would like to watch for changes in the source directory and only process what changed. I know Hadley faced a similar pb with rsmith https://github.com/hadley/rsmith and solved it using shiny reactive "plumbing". I've read the source and I am still not sure how.


The first step is finding which files change to process them. I can do this with a `reactivePoll` on the files size and modification time (in `checkFunc`) but in `valueFunc` I actually have to find again which files changed (because I don't have access to the output of `checkFunc`) and process only those. I'm not sure how that is different from an infinite `while` loop that does (pseudocode)
  old = file.info(dir)
  while ( 0 < 1)
    new = file.info(dir)
    dif = setdiff(new, old)
    process(dif)
    old = new
    sleep(1)
I actually feels less efficient even, since the differences between old and new have to be computed twice.
In Hadley's rsmith, each file is actually "reactive" and this is then put in a higher level `reactivePoll`... but I must admit I don't really follow how the data flows in this code (watch() in https://github.com/hadley/rsmith/blob/master/R/output.R and reactive_file_with_metadata() in https://github.com/hadley/rsmith/blob/master/R/rsmith-file.R).


The second step is probably more tricky. Let us say I have a csv data file which is read by an R file which outputs something. I would like the R process to be run again if the _data_ file changes (with the loop above, it would be run only if the R file itself changes). I am guessing that if I put the data reading in a reactive function and the data processing in another reactive function, I could get the events to be chained. But everything would still start from a request for the output of the processing (which then propagates down). I am not sure how to initiate this from the bottom, when the data changes.
    
I would welcome any pointers. I think this kind of problem is a very nice and broad application for the reactive principles implemented in shiny, even though it is more remote from the core functionality of serving webapps.

Thanks in advance. Sincerely,

*note* In my case it is a static website generator https://github.com/jiho/yssr, but there are many other use cases: source directory of data files and visualisation scripts which produce output graphs, source directory of raw data which gets processed into cleaned data etc.

step 2 - How do I extend this to re-run a processing file that depends on a data file when the _data_ file changes?

parts:
Perhaps your checkFunc could just be this. Shiny willl automatically compare if there are changes.

 checkFunc = function() {
                      new.files <- file.info(dir())
                      new.files
                    } 

The easiest thing I can think of is to have a global variable that stores the previous files values and you compare the

tmp.files <- file.info(dir()) # 

.....

 valueFunc = function() {
                      new.files <- checkFunc()
                      a <- some.user.defined.compare.function(tmp.files, new.files)
                      
                    })
